name: Cart & Checkout Abandonment
goal: Recover started checkouts by answering the questions that stall a millwork order (size, material, delivery, returns, install), giving high-value carts a real person and made-to-order carts an honest, reassuring note.
trigger: Started Checkout (Klaviyo metric trigger from the Miva integration). Fallback: Added to Cart, if Miva cannot send Started Checkout.
flow_filters: Placed Order zero times since starting this flow
Has not been in this flow in the last 7 days
Can receive email marketing; SMS steps also require SMS consent
exit_conditions: Placed Order (any order): exits immediately, all branches
Unsubscribes from email (email steps stop) or replies STOP (SMS steps stop)
smart_sending: Email: OFF for CRT-E1 so it lands about an hour after checkout (the cross-flow exception); ON (16h) for CRT-E2, CRT-E2A, CRT-E2B and CRT-E3. SMS: ON (24h), quiet hours 10am-8pm recipient local time, counts toward the 3-per-7-days SMS cap.

branches.label: High-value cart
branches.rule: Started Checkout value >= $1,000. Checked first, so a high-value cart with made-to-order items lands here (the specialist note covers made-to-order).

branches.label: Made-to-order in cart
branches.rule: Checkout value < $1,000 AND at least one item flagged made-to-order (vinyl shutters, wood shutters, Design Your Own builder items, other made-to-order SKUs).

branches.label: Everyone else
branches.rule: Checkout value < $1,000 and no made-to-order items.

kpis.metric: Placed order rate (per recipient, whole flow)
Branch A reply or call rate (CRT-E2A)

kpis.target: Set baseline in first 30 days, then +10% per quarter

build_notes: Started Checkout must carry: line items (name, SKU, image, URL, size/options, quantity, price), checkout $value, and a per-item made-to-order flag (e.g. is_made_to_order from a Miva product custom field). Without the flag, branch B can't be built; route those carts to Default until it exists.

{{ cart_url }} must restore the cart on any device (a Miva basket-restore or checkout URL passed on the event). If none exists, fall back to https://www.architecturaldepot.com/BASK.html, which only works in the same browser.

Split order: CRT-E1 and CRT-S1 sit above the splits. Before E2, split 1 on value >= 1000 (A), then split 2 on made-to-order (B), else Default. Klaviyo paths don't rejoin, so duplicate CRT-E3 and CRT-S2 into each path with identical content and ids.

CRT-E1's 'Made-to-order pieces in your cart' callout is a show/hide block: show only when the cart has a made-to-order item. Its copy is written conditionally, so it still reads correctly if shown to everyone.

CRT-E2A is a plain-text template: no header, nav or images (keep the required footer). From name: '{{ SPECIALIST_NAME }} at Architectural Depot'. Reply-to must be a monitored inbox (the specialist's or cs@architecturaldepot.com), answered within one business day. Confirm a real, named person before launch; swap in a direct extension if they have one.

{{ CART_INCENTIVE }} is optional and needs approval before launch. If approved: bonus Depot Dollars only (never a percentage off, never a discount on made-to-order items), valid 48 hours from CRT-E3, credited once the order ships. Set a profile property (cart_incentive_expires) so CS can honor it. If not approved, send CRT-E3's no-incentive version.

CRT-S2 is written without the incentive. If {{ CART_INCENTIVE }} is approved, swap to: 'Architectural Depot: Last reminder: order your saved cart in the next 48 hrs to earn [incentive in plain words]. {link} Reply STOP to opt out' and keep it under 160 characters, GSM-7 only.
SMS steps: condition SMS consent = subscribed; quiet hours 10am-8pm local (a text that falls outside waits for the next window).

No 'not in Post-Purchase' filter on purpose: Klaviyo removes a profile the moment it fails a flow filter, so that filter would cancel cart recovery for any repeat buyer within 3 weeks of an order. Smart Sending (16h) spaces Cart and Post-Purchase emails instead.

blocks.text: I'm {{ SPECIALIST_NAME }}, a project specialist at Architectural Depot. Your order is still sitting in your cart, and with a project this size I like to reach out personally before you place it.

On bigger millwork orders, a quick call is often the easiest way to settle the details that matter: lengths and projections, the right material for interior or exterior, the finish, and when everything will arrive.
If anything in your cart is made to order, it's built to your exact size and can't be returned, so I'm glad to go over your measurements with you first.
Just reply with a good time to call, or reach me at 1-888-573-3768 (Mon-Fri 8am-6pm CT, Sat 8am-12pm CT). Your cart is saved whenever you're ready.

Thanks,
{{ SPECIALIST_NAME }}
Project Specialist, Architectural Depot
1-888-573-3768 | cs@architecturaldepot.com

hero.headline: The five questions we hear most before checkout
hero.subhead: If one of these is holding up your order, here's the straight answer.
hero.image: Overhead flat-lay of a project in progress: tape measure, a sketched elevation with dimensions, a corbel and a short moulding profile on a workbench. Natural light.

blocks.text: Hi {{ first_name|default:'there' }}, your cart is still saved. If something is holding you back, it's probably one of these.

items.title: Is it the right size?
items.text: Check the dimensions on the product page against your space: beam span, corbel depth, shutter height. Not sure? Send us your measurements.

items.title: Which material?
items.text: Timberthane faux wood gives you the look of wood, maintenance-free. AmeriCraft is stain-grade real wood. Interior or exterior, tell us where it's going and we'll steer you right.

items.title: When will it ship?
items.text: Heritage Series beams ship in 24-72 hours. Items marked "Free Shipping" ship free to the lower 48 states.

items.title: Can I return it?
items.text: Most items can be returned within 30 days of delivery for a partial refund (20% processing fee; you cover return shipping). Made-to-order items can't be returned.

items.title: How does it install?
items.text: Product pages list the specs, and many include an install guide. Read it before you order so you know what the job takes.
